title: Sweets and snacks
description: Name the sweet things, and say what you like to eat.
grammar: gender and articles, and the words for tastes
grammarNote: Sweet things have their own gender, and some of them are phrases.

explanation.summary: Sweets are a small set of nouns, and they are the first words a learner uses to say what they like. The grammar is the same as everywhere else: a gender, an article, and the plural.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: La galleta, la mermelada, la nata and la patata frita are feminine. El caramelo, el pastel, el chicle, el yogur and el cacahuete are masculine. El cacahuete is a good one to notice: it is a nut in a pod, and it is masculine.

sections.heading: What you like
sections.body: You know how to say what a thing is for, and how to ask for one with un or una: una galleta, un caramelo, un yogur. The plural works the same: las galletas and los caramelos.

items.note: Feminine: la patata frita. You say una patata frita, and las patatas fritas in the plural.

drills.meaning: the biscuits are on the plate

drills.note: Caramelo is masculine, so un caramelo.
